ops.body:
`internal/cli/note_review.go` reimplements freshness verdicts that `notes.Client` already owns (`ReviewNotes`, `ReviewDocs`, `NoteVerdict`, `DocVerdict`). The dead half of that duplication — `reviewDocs`, `docReviewCount`, and, orphaned by their removal, `supersedeDangling` and the `verdictDangling` alias — is now deleted. What remains is live and still duplicated:

- `freshEntity` + `freshFromNote`/`freshFromDoc` — a cli-local projection of the fields `notes` already models.
- `verdictOf` — the EXPIRED > UNVERIFIED > DRIFTED > STALE precedence, a second implementation of `notes.Client`'s.
- `driftedOf` / `liveAnchorOID` / `witnessIndex` — anchor drift detection against live content.
- `noteVerdict` / `docVerdict` — thin projections onto `verdictOf`, called from `internal/cli/print.go` (single-entity `show`) and the doc-verdict tests.
- `witnessIndex` also has non-verdict callers: `internal/cli/dto.go:410,460`.
- `internal/cli/threshold.go` re-declares `noteStaleAfterEnv` / `noteStaleAfterConfig` / `defaultNoteStaleAfter`, duplicating `notes/notes.go:35-37`, because the CLI resolves the threshold from a flag before falling back to config.

Collapsing the rest onto `notes.Client` is roughly a 150-line change and needs the doc/note verdict tests rewritten against the client surface. It was deliberately deferred, not overlooked: the single-entity `show` path wants a verdict for one already-loaded snapshot, which `notes.Client` currently exposes only through `NoteVerdict`/`DocVerdict` taking a resolved `staleAfter` — so the collapse is mostly mechanical but touches every `print.go` call site plus `dto.go`'s witness use.
